dot.accumulators: exact integer, never applied to scales
dot.scale_axis: none or 0 on a rank-2 tensor

device.row_layout: row-padded: every row starts at a 16-byte word; padding lanes are zero trits

M.payload: rows u32, cols u32, format u32 (0 baseline2, 1 dense5)

lines.Y: a = seq << 24 | row, v = y (32-bit two's complement)

z_status.1: refused (configuration, or a region past the store)
z_status.2: ended early (bus words stopped, or aborted)

identity.derivation: sha256('trinity-memory-emulator-v1:' + part)[0:16] for phi, euler, gamma

fpga_chip_info_requires.evidence: all five fields present and well formed

description: JSON-RPC envelope, error codes and HTTP statuses, limits, handles, upload/read/info/delete/dot semantics and the synthetic identity of the emulator. Requests and expected responses are computed from the spec by tools/generate-spec-vectors.py; the TMEM/TensorPack containers use the pure-Python encoders.

replay.backend: a vector with `backend` runs on that backend; for fpga the replay starts the device double of tests/fake_fpga_device.py (tools/bridge_link_protocol.MatvecDevice) on a pseudo-terminal with the vector's `double` options, or a port that does not exist when `double` is {"absent": true}
replay.error_message_contains: with error_code: a substring the error message must contain (which refusal it was, when several share one code)

kinds.rpc: one request body, default or per-vector limits
kinds.sequence: ordered steps on one server; $name substitutes a captured result field

replay.result_at_least: dotted paths to integer counters, or sums of such paths joined by "+", and their lower bounds: counters a stalled process can raise but not lower, such as retransmissions; a sum where a stall can move a count from one counter to another (a nak or bad line read as a late reply)
replay.result_format: keys may be dotted paths into the result

vectors.description: The capability descriptor names the emulator explicitly and reports the configured limits
SDK field names; identities are SHA-256('trinity-memory-emulator-v1:'+part)[0:16]
A null id is a notification, which the Bridge does not implement
The envelope is complete, so the id is echoed
A body above max_request_bytes is refused before parsing
The TMEM count field is checked against max_trits before decoding
TensorPack's decoded-trit limit is a container validation error
The body never completes; after the inactivity timeout the request is invalid JSON
upload -> read (whole, range, tail, out of range) -> info -> dot -> delete on one TMEM container
A 2x3 matrix with per-row scales: exact accumulators, scales returned unapplied
Scales on a contracted axis, rank 3 and scalars are rejected; vectors and scalar-scaled matrices work
An empty TMEM vector is a valid object; its dot with no activations is [0]
Object count and byte limits refuse the second upload; delete reclaims both
Backend fpga: hardware true, transport uart and the configured evidence; the device is not asked
The identity asks the device for its 23 status lines (460 bytes) first; the IDs stay the public synthetic constants and the evidence block identifies the device
The device reports a build id other than the configured evidence
A loader without the matvec extension (protocol 3, the DDR3 loader) is not an fpga backend device
The configured serial port does not exist
upload a TensorPack, dot a dense5 and a baseline2 matrix on the device: exact accumulators, scales unapplied, the image uploaded once and read back, the emulator's sums as reference

steps.description: Retransmissions and repeated runs depend on timing (a stalled host process can cause one), so they are not fixed here; tests/test_bridge_fpga.py checks them
steps.name: dot_dense5

steps.description: The same image is on the device: only the activations and the run go out
steps.name: dot_dense5_again

vectors.description: a corrupted chunk (crc nak), a lost activation ack (the retransmission is answered duplicate), a corrupted Y line (the run is repeated) and a device whose row 1 is 5 too high: the retransmissions are counted and the wrong row is reported under reference, not hidden

steps.description: Each fault forces at least one retransmission or repeated run, and a stalled host process can add more, never fewer: retransmits, matvec_attempts and timeouts (the lost ack never arrives, so at least one attempt of that frame ends at its deadline) are lower bounds. A stall longer than the reply timeout can make the host read the nak or the corrupted Y line while it waits out the retransmission, where it counts as a late reply, so naks and bad_lines are bounded only together with late_replies
steps.name: dot

vectors.description: uploads are held in process memory; the dot fails with a transport error
